retro_skip_reason: DROPPED on your call. Stability reason: R17.55a's amide-bearing precursor is an alpha-amino ALDEHYDE (OHC-CH(NH2)-CONH2), and free alpha-amino aldehydes are never isolated as such - they self-condense as the free base and are sold only as the dimethyl/diethyl acetal, i.e. a protected equivalent, not the compound the rule emits. Its twin R17.55b emits the alpha-amino KETONE instead, which is genuinely sold as the hydrochloride, and R17.55b's record already declares supersedes: [R17.55a], so shipping both would put the weaker twin in competition with the stronger one for the same targets. The retro_smarts I authored for it is preserved below in unauthored_retro_smarts in case you want it back.

The guard is loose, not the chemistry: scoped to a real EWG (ester, nitrile, nitro, sulfonyl) the aza-annulation is legitimate and worth authoring. Tighten the shipped guard to $([#6][#6]=[#8]),$([#6][#6]#[#7]),$([#6][#7](=[#8])[#8]),$([#6][#16](=[#8])=[#8]) - drop the bare $([#6][c]) - and this becomes authorable against e.g. phenylacetonitrile + 1,3-dibromopropane.
